attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, written in his voice.

semantics.note: Firm first clause (AWS spend eats revenue) plus a hedged second clause ('likely billions more'). The 'likely' is kept. The hedged extension cannot be scored on its own; only the firm premise can be.

contract.note: Taking the period from the same post's Jan–Sep 2025 comparison is reasonable. Keeping the cash basis rather than switching to GAAP loss is fair. The contract correctly declines to turn 'likely' into a certain claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no evidence items. Nothing independent establishes Jan–Sep 2025 net AWS payments against estimated revenue, so the firm premise is unchecked. The 'likely billions more' clause is hedged and not scored. With no qualifying evidence, the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own first-person statement in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps the amounts, the Jan–Sep 2025 period, the >100% ratio and the fact that revenue is an estimate.

contract.note: Net AWS cash after credits matches the post's own definition. The denominator is realized revenue, not run rate. These are ordinary readings.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure of run-rate revenue (about $1B in early 2025, over $5B by August). These are annualized figures, not realized nine-month revenue, and say nothing about AWS payments.

reviews.rationale: No independent AWS billing record or reconstruction of realized Jan–Sep 2025 revenue is in the packet. The only item gives run-rate figures, which cannot confirm or refute either the $2.66B or the $2.55B number. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. The cloning remark is a separate assertion and is not scored here.

semantics.note: 'I believe we're going to see' is a plain, unqualified expectation, so it is a scorable forecast. The context makes 'from model providers' a fair addition. The horizon 'next few months' is kept.

contract.note: Six months is a generous reading of 'few months'. Counting only imposed increases, and not optional higher-priced successor models, fits the post's rent-seeking framing. The result does turn on that choice, though.

evidence.note: GPT-5.2 (Dec 2025) costs more per token, but GPT-5.1 stays available in the API. It is an optional successor, not an imposed increase.
GPT-5.4 (Mar 2026) costs more than GPT-5.2. Again an optional successor model, not a mandated increase on existing access.
Sonnet 4.6 kept the same prices. That does not rule out two qualifying increases elsewhere, so it is not real counterevidence.

reviews.rationale: The horizon ended 2026-04-20. The packet shows only optional higher-priced successor models, which the contract does not count, plus one unchanged price. It contains no full record of imposed price increases or negotiated customer terms. Two qualifying increases are neither shown nor ruled out, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own statement in his post.

semantics.note: Limited to the AWS data for Anthropic and Cursor. 'Overall direction of travel' is kept, which softens 'only keep on going up' and allows for monthly drops.

contract.note: Reading 'compute costs' as an aggregate spending trend over each company's stated window is the ordinary meaning in this billing context.

evidence.note: The S-1, available before the cutoff, shows full-year 2025 compute expenses up 190% across all providers. That is a different metric and basis (annual accounting expense, all providers, not monthly AWS cash) and covers Anthropic only.

reviews.rationale: No independently authenticated monthly AWS payment series exists in the packet for either company. The S-1 figures point in the same direction but measure annual, all-provider expense, so they are context only. There is nothing at all for Cursor. Unresolved.
